$comment: Openly-licensed document sources for the parser evaluation corpus.
WHY A MANIFEST RATHER THAN CHECKED-IN FILES: these documents are other people's work under
other people's licences, several hundred megabytes of it. Pinning the commit gives an exactly
reproducible corpus without vendoring a gigabyte of third-party material into this repository
or taking on the redistribution obligations that would come with it.
EVERY SOURCE CARRIES A LICENCE AND IT IS RECORDED HERE. A corpus whose provenance nobody can
state is a corpus nobody can publish a result from.

sources.why: Deliberately constructed PDF pathologies: multi-column LaTeX, AcroForm and LibreOffice forms, rotated/cropped/scaled pages, CMYK and grayscale images, Arabic right-to-left text, PDF/A, annotations, attachments, unreadable metadata.

Real academic papers and the Office formats Nemesis also ingests: DOCX with tables and equations, PPTX decks with speaker notes, XLSX workbooks. The reference set a mature parser tests itself against.

Real-world business and government documents, plus the specific failures a parser meets in the field: multi-column layouts, multi-row/column table cells, embedded CID fonts, rotated pages, invalid PDF structure, Korean text with tables, memos and army forms.

sources.license: CC-BY-4.0 / mixed, per-directory — see the repository's own LICENCE files
sources.why: A digital-preservation corpus: real documents collected because they are awkward. Scans, old producers, damaged files, and formats in versions nobody generates any more.
